answer: A farm running 88 keys therefore forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the river stake is held until the tundra settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the glacier audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 17% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
